problem: NoMaD's goal-masked exploration mode is undirected: with no goal image or map in an unseen environment it wanders, revisits areas and stalls far from the target. NaviDiffusor's point-goal cost guidance injects global info but collapses the action distribution and does not handle unmapped obstacles.
motivation: Classical planners give global awareness while learned diffusion policies give reactivity and generalization; combining them without retraining would be valuable. An overhead camera provides top-down global situational awareness that onboard egocentric cameras lack, but prior overhead-camera systems feed only classical stacks.
key_idea: Plan a global path on a one-time overhead depth-camera occupancy map, convert it into a heading refined by an onboard-depth traversability selector, and steer NoMaD's frozen goal-masked diffusion samples toward that heading via the gradient of a cosine direction cost at inference time.
insight: A heading prior with a cosine cost only rotates steps (gradient roughly perpendicular to each displacement) and skews rather than collapses the sample distribution, so it works better than point-goal guidance (NaviDiffusor baseline: SR 0.33-0.67 vs 1.00 for ODG-NoMaD). The ablation without traversability selection matches the full method in Env-NoObs but has CR 1.00 in Env-RandObs versus 0.00 for the full method, showing the selector is what avoids obstacles unseen by the overhead map.
method: Overhead map and global planner: a single overhead depth frame is back-projected, rotated to the floor frame and classified by height (free/occupied/unknown) into a 0.05 m grid with morphological despeckling; a Nav2 grid planner produces path A->B.
RDP path segmentation: Ramer-Douglas-Peucker simplifies the dense path into near-straight segments; the heading of the segment containing the robot gives the desired direction theta*.

Direction cost: F_dir = -w * sum_i cos(delta_i, d_hat) (w=0.05) over de-normalized cumulative waypoint displacements; its autodiff gradient is applied in the final low-noise DDPM denoising steps with clipping to [-1,1], with the model frozen.

Traversability map: per-frame onboard depth is projected into a robot-centered BEV grid (floor |z|<0.08 m, obstacles 0.1-2 m), obstacles inflated by robot radius and margin, giving free/obstacle/unknown cells.

Two-tier best-direction selector: candidate headings within ±90° of the desired direction are ray-cast (2 m horizon, 1.2 m hard near range with ±0.15 m side rails); obstacle-hitting candidates are rejected, and the rest minimize |phi| + lambda*unknown fraction (rho=1 equals 25°).

Odometry-based direction: the world-frame waypoint direction is rotated into the robot body frame using incrementally tracked pose from a known start; the chosen direction also goes to the low-level controller.

setting.backbone: Pretrained NoMaD diffusion policy (frozen, no retraining) with inference-time gradient guidance
setting.training_data: none additional (uses the pretrained NoMaD checkpoint; guidance is training-free)
setting.observation: onboard monocular RGB (NoMaD) + onboard depth (traversability) on TurtleBot4 OAK-D; one-time overhead ceiling depth camera; odometry
setting.action_space: predicted waypoint trajectories (normalized displacement sequences) from the diffusion policy, tracked by a low-level controller
setting.privileged: Overhead depth camera map of the workspace (used once at deployment), known start position and goal coordinates, odometry

numbers_note: Only a tiny custom Gazebo office benchmark (3 start-goal pairs x 3 runs, per-path results, no aggregate table); no standard benchmark. Split 'test' is a placeholder for the custom setup. The '~7x' residual distance reduction is stated in the abstract/conclusion only.
results: In a small Gazebo office, ODG-NoMaD reaches the goal on all runs (SR 1.00 on every path, both environments) and reduces mean residual distance roughly 7x vs unguided NoMaD, beating NaviDiffusor goal guidance (SR 0.33-0.67). With unmapped obstacles, the full method has CR 0.00 while the variant without the traversability selector has CR 1.00.
limitations: Evaluated only in one small simulated Gazebo office with 3 start-goal pairs and 3 runs each; no real robot, no standard benchmarks.

Requires a single calibrated overhead camera covering the whole bounded workspace, plus known start position and metric goal coordinates, so it is not applicable to truly unseen environments without infrastructure.
Global path is computed once on a static map, and pose relies on odometry drift-prone tracking; dynamic obstacles and larger areas are not addressed.
